title: Perfect
credit: Simple MidiMan arrangement of Ed Sheeran’s Perfect, from Ishay’s sheet — a first real song, not a full engraving. The sheet is in C major, 6/8, and writes both hands in the treble clef; the notes here are at the sheet’s own pitches.
_notation: Per hand, one string per bar. Tokens: pitch (G4, Bb3, C#5), chord [G4 Bb4 D5], rest r. Suffix :n = length in eighths (default 1; fractions like 1/2 and dotted values like 1.5 allowed). Prefix ~ = tied from the previous token of the same pitch (no new attack). Prefix / = rolled chord. This song is 6/8: every bar must sum to 6 eighths. The beat is the dotted quarter (two beats a bar).

sections.name: Theme
sections.hint: The tune everyone knows. Right hand starts on E and falls to C; left hand climbs the same four chords — C, A minor, F, G — two bars each. Bars 7 and 15 are one long held D.
sections.coach: E, E — then down to C. The left hand climbs the same four chords all the way.

sections.name: Bridge
sections.hint: The chords now change every bar — A minor, F, C, G, four times round. The right hand answers an octave higher, in long-short pairs: a dotted eighth then a sixteenth tied on.
sections.coach: Chords move twice as fast now. A minor, F, C, G — round four times.

sections.name: Theme 2
sections.hint: The tune comes back exactly as it started, and there is a repeat sign at the end of bar 40 — on the sheet you go back to the top. Bars 41–42 walk both hands down out of it.
sections.coach: The tune again, then walk it down.

sections.name: Outro
sections.hint: The arpeggio stops. Left hand holds long notes and takes over the line while the right hand rolls up; the last C major chord is held over two bars.
sections.coach: Long notes now. End on C major.
